title: Astrid and the Oath
premise: Ulyana Delacroix, a runaway apprentice hiding a small, stubborn gift, keeps the ledgers of the Vesper Guild, which trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, one dying dragon's last flame. When the crown's witch-hunt reaches the city, Ulyana discovers the ledgers conceal a covenant: the guild has sheltered gifted folk for centuries by binding their power into the dragon-fire, and that fire is guttering out. Hunted by an inquisitor who was once Ulyana's closest friend, and torn between loyalty to the found family of the guild and the truth that exposing the covenant could save them or reignite the ancient war between crown and dragons, Ulyana must choose. In the end, Ulyana feeds their own gift into the last flame—not to hide it, but to make it a hearth the whole city can warm at—and the guild steps out of shadow as the kingdom's first open house of magic.
about_author: Astrid Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from forgotten port cities before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep secrets in ink and find family in unlikely places.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A night of inventory at the Vesper Guild: bottled thunder, a widow's borrowed year, a scale of living ember. Ulyana hides a flicker of their own gift while balancing accounts, establishing the guild as scrappy found family. Emotional beat: belonging purchased with secrecy.

chapters.title: Apprentice No More
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback woven through present. How they fled hedge-witch Maren's cottage after a healing went wrong and a village turned fearful. The guild took them in without questions. Beat: guilt over the past shaping loyalty to the present.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Market Cross
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Criers announce the crown's hunt: all gifted persons must register or burn. The guild goes quiet, ledgers hidden, wards doubled. Old dragon-keeper Bram says only, 'It's starting again.' Beat: safety curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's White Gloves
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Sera Vance's POV. She arrives in the city hunting a 'ledger-keeper' rumored to traffic in magic. We learn she once loved someone with the gift and lost them to it. Beat: the hunter given a human face.

chapters.title: What the Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He tends the last dragon, Ember-of-Endings, ancient and nearly out of flame. He reveals to Ulyana that the guild's impossible goods are powered by gifts bound into the fire—a covenant older than the crown. Beat: awe and burden of inherited secret.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Storms
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A client defaults on a bottled storm; retrieving it forces Ulyana to use their gift publicly for the first time in years. Someone sees. Beat: the thrill of being seen warring with terror.

chapters.title: Sera Finds a Thread
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Following the storm incident, she traces rumors to the Vesper quarter. She interviews frightened neighbors, torn between duty and memory of her lost friend. Beat: sympathy sharpening into pursuit.

chapters.title: The Covenant Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Bram shows them the original covenant pages hidden inside the oldest ledger: the guild shelters the gifted, the fire holds their power, and when the fire dies, every bound gift breaks loose at once. Beat: horror—the family's foundation is a countdown.

chapters.title: Maren at the Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Their old teacher arrives seeking sanctuary, hunted herself, carrying word that other hedge-witches are being taken north. Reunion is tender and barbed; old wounds reopen. Beat: forgiveness offered but not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Ledgers Burned, Names Kept
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Odile's POV. She orders the client ledgers destroyed to protect everyone listed, keeping only names memorized. Ulyana protests—history matters—but learns some truths must be carried in people, not paper. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Ember-of-Endings falters; a bound gift snaps free in the city—a child levitating a cart in broad daylight. Panic spreads; the hunt intensifies. Beat: the countdown accelerates beyond control.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Warrants
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She identifies Ulyana from the storm incident and realizes the ledger-keeper is someone she knew as children. She delays filing the warrant, buying days she shouldn't. Beat: love complicating duty.

chapters.title: The War Nobody Wants Again
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Researching the first dragon war in sealed archives: the crown burned the dragons' roosts; the dragons' allies broke the sky. If the fire dies unbound, the same powers return leaderless. Beat: stakes widen from personal to apocalyptic.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Vesper Quarter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A guild member, terrified for his registered daughter, sells the guild's location to save her. The raid comes at dawn. Beat: betrayal born of love, not malice.

chapters.title: Smoke Over the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The raid: wards fail, Maren is captured covering the others' escape, Bram stays behind with the dragon. Ulyana flees into the undercity with the covenant pages and the child whose gift broke loose. Beat: grief and flight.

chapters.title: Undercity Parley
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera corners Ulyana beneath the city. Instead of arresting them, she demands the whole truth—and gets it: the covenant, the dying fire, the coming unbinding. Beat: enemy becomes reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Price of the Flame
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The covenant can be renewed, but only by a willing gift freely given—permanently surrendered into the fire. Ulyana volunteers; Sera and the escaped guild members refuse to let them. Beat: sacrifice proposed, contested.

chapters.title: Storming the Pyre Court
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. To reach Ember-of-Endings, held captive in the crown's pyre court where captured gifted await burning, the group infiltrates during a public sentencing. Maren is on the pyre list. Beat: desperate rescue, rising action cresting.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire and Crown-Iron
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax part one: the rescue erupts; Bram falls freeing the dragon; Sera openly defies her order, burning her own warrant. Ember-of-Endings rises, weak but awake. Beat: losses that make victory costly.

chapters.title: The Last Gift Given
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax part two: before the unbinding can tear the city apart, Ulyana gives their gift to the fire willingly—not erased, but transformed into a hearth-flame that steadies every bound gift instead of caging it. The covenant is rewritten aloud, witnessed by crowd and crown. Beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: Terms of a New Peace
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aftermath: the crown, facing a risen dragon and a united guild, negotiates. Registration becomes sanctuary; the pyre court closes. Sera takes charge of the new accord, honoring the friend she lost by protecting those like them. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: A Hearth, Not a Hiding Place
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Epilogue: the guild reopens openly, its ledgers now public record; Maren teaches apprentices in the front room; the hearth-flame warms anyone who enters. Ulyana, giftless but not diminished, writes the first honest entry. Beat: belonging chosen, not hidden.
